title: Immediate Yerevan protest and entry into government buildings after ceasefire announcement
scope: Yerevan; locations within one city, no national organization established for this immediate action
organizer: Unknown; accounts describe crowds reacting immediately to the announcement

threshold_50_evidence.summary: RFE/RL photo captions show crowds gathering at Republic Square and parliament and entering state buildings, but do not report a reliable simultaneous headcount. A search-only Euronews result describes hundreds; that snippet is discovery only and not used to establish the threshold.

start_date.summary: RFE/RL dates the government-building and parliament entry to the early hours of Nov 10.

location.summary: Photo captions identify Republic Square, government headquarters and parliament in Yerevan.

demands.summary: Captions describe anger and betrayal over the PM's decision to end fighting; the exact requested remedy at this immediate crowd is not specified. Political-policy demand is preliminary.

participants.summary: No body-read source gives an attendance estimate for the immediate crowd.

threshold_50.summary: Crowds are visible/described, but no body-read simultaneous count proves 50; pending threshold.

protester_violence.summary: Captions report protesters rampaging/vandalizing offices, throwing objects and attacking the parliamentary speaker, who was hospitalized.

state_response.summary: The reviewed photo captions do not establish a government response; all response values remain unknown.

end_date.summary: No reviewed source establishes when this immediate action ended.

notes: This immediate post-announcement action is kept distinct from the opposition coalition's organized rallies beginning Nov 11. The captured RFE/RL gallery provides caption evidence only. A separate search-result headline calls the crowd hundreds, but is not used as body evidence. The exact remedy sought by the first crowd, size and duration remain unresolved.
open_questions: Was at least 50 people present simultaneously in a public gathering pressing a clearly stated demand to Armenia's government?
Did participants explicitly demand annulment/revision of the agreement or only express anger?
When did this immediate action end, and how is it distinct from the organized rallies starting Nov 11?

title: 17-party opposition rally and march demanding Pashinyan resignation
scope: Single physically reported public action in Yerevan; related dates are recorded separately pending continuity evidence.
organizer: Opposition parties; contemporary accounts identify a 17-party coalition
participants_original: Thousands at the rally; several hundred marched to the National Assembly on Nov 11

threshold_50_evidence.summary: RFE/RL and Public Radio of Armenia describe thousands at the Nov 11 rally; RFE/RL says several hundred marched to the National Assembly. These are qualitative body reports, not exact bounds.

start_date.summary: RFE/RL and Public Radio of Armenia describe the coalition rally on Nov 11; Armenpress separately says the same parties also held a rally on Nov 12.

location.summary: Only the specific locations reported for this dated action are recorded.

organizer.summary: Opposition parties; contemporary accounts identify a 17-party coalition

demands.summary: The listed demand is attributed only to this dated action.

participants.summary: Thousands at the rally; several hundred marched to the National Assembly on Nov 11

threshold_50.summary: RFE/RL and Public Radio of Armenia describe thousands at the Nov 11 rally; RFE/RL says several hundred marched to the National Assembly. These are qualitative body reports, not exact bounds.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed reports do not establish protester violence for this dated action.

state_response.summary: Nov 11 reporting records detentions and police warnings/efforts to stop this gathering; no Nov 12 or later response is carried over.

end_date.summary: The sources date this specific rally/march to Nov 11; this event record ends with the dated action, not the broader campaign.

notes: This is the Nov 11 action only. Nov 12, Nov 18 and Nov 19 actions are separate candidates; related opposition affiliation does not establish continuous physical protest.
open_questions: Was attendance at one simultaneous Nov 11 public gathering at least 50?

organizer: Supporters of opposition group Sasna Tsrer

organizer.summary: The report identifies supporters of Sasna Tsrer as organizers/participants.

location.summary: The article says the group rallied in central Yerevan.

demands.summary: The article does not specify what demand this separate rally made.

participants.summary: No number or threshold estimate is reported.

state_response.summary: Police told the group to disband under martial law; a number who refused were detained. No other response dimension is established.

notes: Kept distinct from the 17-party coalition rally because RFE/RL explicitly describes Sasna Tsrer supporters as a separate gathering and says their march was cancelled. Police dispersal/detentions are attributed only to this group. The source does not identify the rally’s own demand or number present.
open_questions: Did this separate rally have a qualifying demand directed at Armenia's government or policy?
Were at least 50 present simultaneously?
Is this part of the larger anti-ceasefire campaign or a distinct action?

title: Families of missing servicemen rally outside Armenia's Defence Ministry seeking answers
scope: Yerevan; ministry-side gathering and separately reported movement to Russian Embassy not merged without review
organizer: Parents and relatives of Armenian servicemen missing during the Nagorno-Karabakh war

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The exact-date APA/Sputnik Armenia report says relatives were rallying outside the Defence Ministry and demanding a meeting, but reports no attendance. Threshold remains unknown.

start_date.summary: APA reports on Nov 23 that the gathering was taking place; whether it began earlier in the month is not specified in this usable report.

location.summary: The reported gathering was in front of the Armenian Ministry of Defence in Yerevan.

organizer.summary: Parents and relatives of servicemen missing in the war are identified as protesters.

demands.summary: Protesters sought a meeting with the former Defence Minister to obtain answers about missing servicemen, a demand directed to Armenian state officials.

threshold_50.summary: No simultaneous attendance estimate; pending threshold.

state_response.summary: An Armenian MP appeared and said the issue would be discussed by government later that day; the article does not establish a formal negotiation, response completion or other coded state action.

notes: APA article explicitly says it cites Sputnik Armenia; do not count the two outlets as independent confirmations. A later-dated RFE/RL story and CivilNet story were accidentally body-rendered without the required prior exact-URL checks; their content is not used and is documented as a protocol deviation.
open_questions: Were at least 50 relatives gathered simultaneously on Nov 23?
Was the November 23 action a distinct event or part of a multi-day gathering that began earlier in the month?
Was an actual meeting held and were the missing-servicemen demands addressed?
